title: Colorado Upsets No. 14 Houston 42-32 and Keeps Its Bowl Hopes Alive
dek: Colorado rushed for 249 yards and scored 21 points in the second quarter in a Friday night win at Folsom Field that ended Houston’s Big 12 title hopes.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The exterior of Folsom Field, the University of Colorado stadium in Boulder

keyPoints: Colorado beat No. 14 Houston 42-32 on Friday night, Nov. 13, at Folsom Field in Boulder, The Gazette reported. The win ended Houston’s Big 12 title hopes.
After the first quarter Houston had 143 total yards to Colorado’s 13, Buffaloes Wire reported. Colorado then scored 21 points in the second quarter and took a 21-20 lead into halftime.

Colorado scored a season-high 42 points, the most against a Big 12 opponent since a 52-0 win over Oklahoma State nearly two years ago, The Gazette reported. Buffaloes Wire reported 249 rushing yards, the most of any Colorado game this season.
Colorado must win its final two games, against Cincinnati and UCF, to keep its bowl hopes alive, Buffaloes Wire reported.
body:
Colorado beat No. 14 Houston 42-32 on Friday night at Folsom Field in Boulder, keeping its bowl hopes alive and ending Houston’s Big 12 title hopes, [The Gazette reported](https://gazette.com/2026/11/14/winning-formula-finally-shows-in-colorados-upset-of-no-14-houston).

## A slow start, then a turn

Houston controlled the early game. [Buffaloes Wire reported](https://coloradobuffaloeswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/buffaloes/football/2026/11/14/colorado-houston-football-takeaways-upset-win-week-11/92777644007) that after the first quarter Houston had 143 total yards to Colorado’s 13, and a clear edge in time of possession and rushing yards. Colorado changed the game in the second quarter, scoring 21 points and taking a 21-20 lead into halftime.

## Running game and explosive plays

Colorado finished with 249 rushing yards, the most of any game this season, Buffaloes Wire reported. The Buffaloes are 4-1 this season when they rush for at least 180 yards. Buffaloes Wire said the biggest difference from Colorado’s other wins was the number of explosive plays. The team held the ball for fewer than 10 minutes in the first half, but its first-half touchdowns came from more than 30 yards out. Richard Young is the team’s primary back, Buffaloes Wire reported.

## Defence holds on

Houston scored only 12 points in the second half, Buffaloes Wire reported, and Colorado made two stops on Houston two-point attempts. The Gazette reported that the defence got enough stops and turnovers from its key players to hold off one of the better offences in the country. DeAndre Moore’s 34-yard punt return set up a touchdown late in the first half, The Gazette reported.

## Context for Colorado

Colorado had lost to Arizona State the week before. Buffaloes Wire reported that the loss had seemed to end the team’s bowl hopes. The Gazette reported that the 42 points were the season high and the most the program has scored against a Big 12 opponent since a 52-0 win over Oklahoma State nearly two years ago. Coach Deion Sanders told The Gazette: “We all caught the same bus.”

## What comes next

Colorado still has games against Cincinnati and UCF. Buffaloes Wire reported that the Buffaloes must win both to keep their bowl hopes alive. Buffaloes Wire also reported that Houston needed the win to keep its own playoff hopes alive.

Meridian has not independently verified the game statistics beyond the reporting cited here.
